cleanIntro: The 695 is a bolt gun that happens to fire slugs, and it strips like one: safety cap to ON, bolt back, trigger held, bolt out. The safety is a CAP that rotates counterclockwise rather than a button that slides, which is worth knowing before you go looking for a tang switch that is not there.

steps.title: Safety cap fully counterclockwise to ON
steps.action: Rotate the safety cap fully to the left — counterclockwise — to ON, and keep the muzzle pointed somewhere harmless. It is a cap, not a sliding button.
steps.quote: Rotate the safety cap fully to the left (counterclockwise) to the “ON” (SAFE) position (Fig. 1); keep the muzzle pointed in a safe direction.
steps.cite: MODEL 695 BOLT ACTION SLUG SHOTGUN — Mossberg owner's manual — Model 695 owner's manual — TO REMOVE THE BOLT

steps.title: Bolt handle up, bolt fully back, then look
steps.action: Raise the bolt handle and pull the bolt back as far as it goes, then inspect and remove all ammunition from the magazine and chamber.
steps.quote: Raise the bolt handle and pull back bolt as far as it will go. Inspect and remove all ammunition in the magazine or chamber.
steps.cite: MODEL 695 BOLT ACTION SLUG SHOTGUN — Mossberg owner's manual — Model 695 owner's manual — TO REMOVE THE BOLT

steps.title: Re-check chamber and magazine
steps.action: Check both again before anything comes out of the gun. On a bolt shotgun the magazine is easy to leave loaded while the chamber is clear.
steps.quote: Re-check the chamber and magazine to be certain gun is unloaded.
steps.cite: MODEL 695 BOLT ACTION SLUG SHOTGUN — Mossberg owner's manual — Model 695 owner's manual — TO REMOVE THE BOLT

steps.title: ⛔ Hold the TRIGGER back and draw the bolt out — this is correct
steps.action: With the gun proven empty and pointed somewhere safe, hold the trigger back and pull the bolt handle rearward to release the bolt assembly from the receiver. Holding a trigger deliberately feels wrong and is exactly what this action requires — which is why the gun must be proven empty twice before you do it.
steps.quote: Hold the trigger back and pull the bolt handle to the rear to release the bolt assembly from the receiver.
steps.cite: MODEL 695 BOLT ACTION SLUG SHOTGUN — Mossberg owner's manual — Model 695 owner's manual — TO REMOVE THE BOLT

deepAbsentReason: The 695 book publishes bolt removal and cleaning and nothing deeper. ⛔ No further path is invented for it.

cleaning.name: BORE, CHAMBER AND BOLT
tasks: Solvent and brush through bore and chamber, patches until clean
Bolt face, extractor and locking lug recesses
A light film of oil on the bolt body where it rides the raceway
⛔ Nothing left in the bore — a slug barrel obstructs like any other
cleaning.quote: Your firearm should be inspected and cleane
cleaning.src: MODEL 695 BOLT ACTION SLUG SHOTGUN — Mossberg owner's manual, CLEANING AND LUBRICATION

reassembly: Safety cap ON. Bolt back into the raceway, handle up.
Push the bolt fully forward and turn the handle down to lock.
Cycle it several times to feel it run free.
Function test before it is put away.
fncheck: Chamber and magazine proven empty. Open and close the bolt several times to check free movement. Close it with the safety cap ON and pull the trigger — the firing pin should NOT release. Finger off, rotate the cap to FIRE — it should still not release on its own. Then pull the trigger and it should. ⛔ Make sure no cleaning patch is left in the barrel before it is loaded.
